The central claim of the paper is that both proposed models outperform their corresponding parameter-matched baselines, with GRURNTN producing the strongest overall results.
In GRURNTN, the tensor product is applied between the current input and the reset-gated previous hidden state when computing the candidate hidden layer.
In LSTMRNTN, the tensor product is applied between the current input and the previous hidden layer when computing the candidate memory cell.
